maya: FYI I hacked up a 'transfer-token' flow for multi-region primary handoffs to reduce full-escrow cost. High level: issue short-lived signed token referencing last-committed-seq; receiver validates then requests claim. If claim completes, ownership flips. No snapshot transfer unless needed.
jordan: solid if it reduces egress, but what about correctness? how do we avoid split-brain and lost acked writes?
maya: plan: origin keeps serving reads until claim final. target can accept writes in 'proxy-forward' mode: local apply + mirror to origin for durability until claim finishes. If claim fails, local writes are tombstoned or reconciled per policy.
sam: important: every write must have an immutable audit record so billing/compliance safe. token lifecycle events too.
maya: yes 100%  token.create/query/accept/abort -> audit index with trace ids. retention/export part of RFC.
elio: TTL and GC interaction? tokens expiring while origin GC-ed would break assumptions.
maya: default TTL=90s, configurable 30s 10m. we gate issuance if cluster GC horizon < ttl + safety_margin.
jordan: operator UX: what states are visible in console? oncall needs concise names.
maya: states: TOKEN_PENDING, TOKEN_ACCEPTED, TOKEN_ABORTED, TOKEN_ROLLBACK. ops-bot emits transitions.
ops-bot: automsg  transfer-token created tenant=acme id=tx-992 ttl=90s trace=tx-992
sam: compatibility: if target can't verify token (older control-plane), fallback to full escrow so cutover still works.
elio: runtime upgrade scenario? mix of old/new nodes might mis-handle token verification.
maya: safety shim: control-plane compatibility check at issuance time. If cluster has old nodes, we refuse token issuance and force escrow. Also offer operator override.
jordan: perf model? when is token path worth it vs escrow?
maya: quick local numbers: small-tenant case (<30 qps, state <3MB) reduces median cutover ~8s -> ~0.8s and egress by ~93%. large/high-QPS tenants still prefer escrow.
sam: testing: simnet chaos with cross-region blackhole while doing frequent transfers. Verify no acknowledged writes lost and tail latency within SLO.
elio: add conflict/claim response shape: {accepted, conflicting_seq, retry_after} so receiver can reason about retries.
maya: will include proto sketch and event schema in RFC. also include operator runbook and failure diagrams.
jordan: one more: per-tenant opt-out feature flag and cluster-wide circuit-breaker if we see claim failure rates spike.
maya: agreed. I'll draft RFC and a small gRPC proto + ops-bot hooks. will ping infra/devex when ready. :thumbsup:
